intro.title: Build long task profiler using performance API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple profiler that detects and logs long-running tasks in a web application using the Performance API. You will learn how to use the PerformanceObserver interface to monitor performance entries and identify tasks that block the main thread. The core programming concepts involved include event listeners, callbacks, and basic conditionals to filter performance data. By the end, you'll have a working tool that helps you understand and improve your app's responsiveness.
intro.usecase: Long task profiling is essential for optimizing performance in data-intensive web applications like analytics dashboards and financial platforms. Developers use the Performance API to identify JavaScript execution bottlenecks that cause UI freezes in interactive elements such as complex data tables, real-time charts, and multi-step forms. By monitoring long tasks, teams can improve responsiveness in products like Google Analytics, trading interfaces, or collaborative editing tools where smooth user interaction is critical. This pattern helps maintain 60fps rendering and meet Core Web Vitals thresholds for better user retention and SEO rankings.
